title: Structural clean-up of _engine.py and the stroke runner
description:
The improvement pass merged in PR #14 left `oilpaint/_engine.py` at about 3,900 lines. The code-quality audit's structural findings for the engine and the stroke runner were deferred so they would not collide with the speed work. That work is merged, so they can be done now. This comes first because both remaining paint features (ploughing/marbling, dry-brush over relief) change `brush_step_on`.

Findings still to check against the current code and do (the audit predates the split of `brush.py` into `brush.py`, `stroke.py`, `_knife.py`, `_geometry.py`, `_hair.py`, so find things by name, not by line):

- `_Run.__init__` does five jobs: sampling the stroke, building textures, radii, knife set-up, stroke constants. Split into module-level functions; keep the random-draw order. Drop state that is never read.
- `_Run.step` builds geometry and also spends paint off the canvas. Separate the two.
- `_knife_step` has seven numbered stages in one function. One function per stage; the order the stages change the canvas must stay. Stop passing bare booleans positionally to `lay` and `spread`; fix the misleading parameter names of `flow_under_blade` (`lateral`, `half`).
- `brush_step_on` (cyclomatic complexity about 40): extract njit helpers for the marked stages (drag fraction, column thickness, plough, contact and catch, lay thickness, off-canvas use, stir fraction).
- `footprint`, `level`, `flow_under_blade`, `deposit`: split by phase; replace `deposit`'s three booleans by a mode; one `_bury` helper for the "old top goes under by a share k" loop that is written out in `deposit`, `settle_pending` and `merge_same`.
- `Step` has 38 fields mixing window, motion, hold and carried brush state; the array bundles (`cv`, `aux`, `br`, `taps`, `ridges`, `pend`) are plain tuples read by index. Use nested and named tuples.
- Duplicated helpers (smoothstep, box blur, bilinear sampling, film coverage, Kubelka-Munk `B`/`tau`, per-column demand) and duplicated or unnamed constants (`MIN_FILM`, dab span 1.3, swap rates, volume per amount, `level` iterations, spatter and lighting numbers).
- `brush`/`stroke` code reads `Canvas` private attributes; give `Canvas` a small engine view instead.
- Indirection that hides errors: `_Step.__getattr__`, `Brush.clean()` calling `__init__`, `ALL` built from `globals()`, shared module-level arrays not marked read-only.
acceptance_criteria:
- Painted state stays bit-identical: `python tools/bench.py --compare` against a baseline saved before the change reports all 16 scenes identical.
- Speed within noise of the baseline on `tools/bench.py` (extra array returns and recompiled kernels measured, not assumed).
- `tox` passes (tests, coverage, black, ruff, pyright, spell-check); the ruff complexity exemption for `_engine.py` is removed or narrowed.
notes:
Plan: three stages, each bit-identical against a saved bench baseline. 1) split the oversized kernels in _engine.py; 2) Python side (stroke.py, _knife.py, Canvas engine view, duplicated helpers and constants, indirections); 3) named tuples for Step and the array bundles. Opus 5.5 medium agents implement and review; the orchestrator verifies and merges.
Stage 1 done (commit a1a6de7): every function in _engine.py at or under complexity 13, ruff exemption for the file removed, all 16 bench scenes identical, cold compile 47 s vs 43 s. Split helpers are inline="always". Stage 2 (Python side: stroke.py, _knife.py, Canvas engine view) next.
Stage 2 done: stroke set-up split into module-level functions, knife kernel calls by keyword, Canvas relief maps in one _Relief with read-only view properties (pickle layout unchanged), shared _coverage/_km_terms, engine constants, explicit ALL lists, read-only tables. Paint and renders byte-identical; 587 tests. Stage 3 (named tuples for Step and the array bundles) next.
Stage 3 done (commit e642a7c): Layers/Beneath/Load/Pending/Taps/Ridges named tuples read by field; Step(win, motion, hold); brush_step takes a plain kit once per stroke and names it on entry (numba resolves named tuples more slowly per call). make pre-push passes: tox on py3.11-3.15, wheel, coverage 81.4%, spelling; 589 tests. Not done by decision: deposit keeps its three boolean flags (independent, four combinations in use); settle_pending's and the hold-back's burials stay separate (different arithmetic); StrokeConsts and the chord tables stay flat/plain (per-call cost).
close_reason: All three stages merged on ccr-77a655e0-ewp724: kernels split (complexity <= 13, ruff exemption for _engine.py removed), Python side tidied, bundles and Step named. All 16 bench scenes byte-identical to the pre-change baseline, renders byte-identical, speed within noise, cold compile +8%, tox green on every Python.

title: Ploughing and marbling through thick wet paint
description:
Paint audit mechanism R7, not built in PR #14. A loaded brush pushed hard through thick wet paint should cut grooves into it, leave the old paint standing between the grooves, and lay the new colour into them, which gives the marbled look of wet-in-wet work. Today the brush rides on its own load and stirs the two paints evenly, so about 85-90% of a blue bed is left untouched under a white stroke at pressure 0.9 and the core of the stroke is nearly uniform.

Design from the audit (in `brush_step_on`):
1. Bristle level `gap(p, stiffness)` above the floor, independent of the brush's own load.
2. Cut deeper along clump lines (low `hair`); leave old paint standing between them.
3. The side share of ploughed paint grows with pressure and stiffness (it is a fixed 35% today); lay new paint into the grooves with weight `1 - hair`.
4. Replace `stir` here with a lane-wise fold: full exchange in groove lanes, none in ridge lanes.

Apply only above about pressure 0.4 and on wet paint thicker than about 1.5 units, so that "white over wet sky stays white" survives.
acceptance_criteria:
- Blue left under a white stroke at pressure 0.9: under 60% (today about 85-90%), with ridges at least 1.3x the bed.
- Luminance standard deviation across the stroke core at pressure 0.6 and above: at least 0.08 and rising with pressure (today 0.024-0.026).
- Regression scenes `blending`, `dirty_brush` and the Bob Ross example checked by metrics and amplified difference images, not by eye alone.
- Pigment is conserved; `tox` passes; speed measured with `tools/bench.py`.

title: tools/bench.py --compare does not cover the rendered picture
description: tools/bench.py --save/--compare fingerprints the painted state (wet layers, coverage, dried height, relief maps, rng state, stroke counter, brush loads) but never renders. A change confined to canvas compositing, spectral.py or _render.py therefore passes --compare whatever it does to the picture. In oilpaint-b63 stage 2 the rendering side had to be proved with a one-off script that compared render(), reflectance(), color_at(), surface_height() and the Kubelka-Munk functions between two trees. To do: let the bench also record, per scene, the bytes of the lit and unlit render and of surface_height() (as extra keys in the saved state or behind a flag such as --render, so the timing of the painting itself is not disturbed), and compare them bytewise like the rest. Keep old saved states comparable or say clearly that they must be re-saved.
acceptance_criteria: A deliberate one-bit change in _render.shade or canvas compositing is reported by --compare; the painting timings are unaffected by the extra work; CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md convention line still holds as written.

title: Cached render kernels can go stale when spectral.py changes
description: numba's on-disk cache for a kernel is keyed on the modification time and size of the kernel's own source file, and globals from other modules are frozen into the compiled code. _render.py compiles N_BANDS from spectral.py into its cached kernels with no guard of its own; the _compiled_packed check in _engine.py only protects _render when _engine.py is unchanged. If spectral.WAVELENGTHS (and so N_BANDS) changes without _render.py changing, a stale cached kernel could be loaded. Found in the review of oilpaint-b63 stage 2 (which is why _dab.SPAN duplicates _engine.DAB_SPAN, pinned by a test). To do: list every cross-module global read inside a cached kernel (_engine.py, _render.py, _dab.py and any other njit code), and give each either a local copy pinned by a test or a guard like _compiled_packed that fails loudly when the compiled value differs from the current one.
acceptance_criteria: Every global from another module used inside a cache=True kernel is either duplicated locally with an equality test or checked at import against the compiled value; a test demonstrates the guard for _render.

title: Dry-brush should catch dried crests and skip the hollows
description:
Paint audit mechanism R11, not built in PR #14. A nearly dry brush dragged lightly over dried impasto should leave paint only on the crests it touches and skip the hollows (scumbling). Today the deposit does not follow dried relief at furrow scale: the correlation between a scumble and the dry relief under it is -0.14.

Design from the audit:
- Give the tips a height: `tip_level = local mean surface + reach(p, stiffness)`; scale the deposit by how far a point lies below it, more strongly at low pressure and low load.
- This needs a second "below local mean" map at furrow scale (blur 4-6 px) beside `_hollows` in `canvas.py`, rebuilt at `dry()`.
- Confine it to pressure under about 0.35.
acceptance_criteria:
- Correlation between scumble deposit and the dry relief under it: at least +0.3 (today -0.14).
- Strokes at pressure 0.35 and above are unchanged (bit-identical on the scenes that do not scumble).
- `tox` passes; speed measured with `tools/bench.py`.

title: Colour bands of a double-loaded brush should wander with the furrows
description:
A double-loaded brush (two or more colours side by side on the tip) lays straight colour bands, while the furrows left by the hairs wander, merge and split along the stroke since PR #14. The colour boundaries should follow the same 2-D hair field as the relief, so that the bands drift with the furrows instead of running ruler-straight through them.

Best done together with ploughing and marbling, which reworks how lanes exchange paint.

title: Lifted multi-colour dab drifts a few percent in one pigment
description:
Known limit left by PR #14: when a brush loaded with several colours is dabbed and lifted, the amount of one pigment can end up a few percent off what the brush gave up. Single-colour dabs and drawn strokes conserve pigment.

Find where the lift-off or the dab mound shares paint between colours without conserving each pigment separately (`_lift_off`, dab mounds), and add a conservation test for a multi-colour dab.

title: One-pixel crests at shallow slants still bead in the highlights
description: Known limit left by PR #14: highlights are now gathered along narrow crests, but a crest that is one pixel wide and runs at a shallow slant to the pixel grid still shows as a string of beads at the pixel steps instead of a continuous glint.

title: A few footprint-edge pixels are still sensitive to rounding
description:
Known limit left by PR #14: under a clean brush or knife, a few pixels at the edge of the footprint can still flip between covered and empty depending on rounding in the last bit (for example between CPUs). PR #14 removed most of this by making coverage use the `EMPTY` threshold; the remaining cases are at footprint edges.

Low priority: the effect is a handful of pixels and is not visible in renders, but it limits bit-exact comparison across machines.
